hourly.summary: Manchester United fans are enduring a full-blown meltdown: worst start since 1986, a five-year Champions League away win drought, a £1.15bn debt mountain, and a 4-4 draw with Villa after conceding two in three minutes. Pochettino's reign began with a drubbing at Anfield (down to ten men after eight minutes), while Sporting Lisbon are 75% favourites to beat them in the UCL. The only thing getting a standing ovation at the Etihad was Kevin De Bruyne — while former United man Hojlund got booed. The Glazers' leveraged buyout bill (£886m in interest alone) looms larger than any transfer budget.

daily.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained catastrophically low throughout the day, anchored by a 4-0 opening-day hammering at Anfield that left the club in the relegation zone. The morning's frantic 'meltdown' — questioning Pochettino's tactics, Mount's display, and INEOS's recruitment — hardened by evening into a grim, resigned 'doomed' narrative, with fans citing the board's bureaucratic transfer process and a brutal fixture list as proof the season is already lost. No meaningful recovery in mood occurred; the dominant arc is from panic to hopeless acceptance.

weekly.summary: The week began with resigned scepticism around Pochettino's appointment, spiked into brief hopeful excitement at his arrival, then plummeted catastrophically after a 4-0 Anfield thrashing left United 19th with the worst defense in Europe. Sentiment collapsed from a mid-week high of 7/10 to back-to-back 2/10 lows, shifting from 'rebounding' optimism to 'meltdown' and 'catastrophic' despair as relegation talk, structural implosion narratives, and total leadership distrust dominated.
